reconcile.note: John Gill distinguishes God being tried or provoked by evil people, which he concedes, from being enticed toward evil, which James's denial actually targets.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Can God be tempted?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/tempt_god.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: You shall not tempt Yahweh your God, as you tempted him in Massah.
sides.verseText: You shall not tempt Yahweh your God, as you tempted him in Massah.

sides.snippet: for God can't be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one
sides.verseText: Let no man say when he is tempted, \"I am tempted by God,\" for God can't be tempted by evil, and he himself tempts no one.
